proposals.current: Merges each greyscale image plane into a multi-channel image. Implements the standard ImageJ algorithm for merging channels that either creates an RGB or a composite image. We recommend to use Blend images for creating renders and Merge channels (composite) that provide more options for the specific use cases. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Merges each greyscale image plane into a multi-channel image using the classic ImageJ merge channels algorithm, which creates an RGB or a composite image. We recommend to use Blend images for creating renders and Merge channels (composite) that provide more options for the specific use cases. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Applies 'Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization' (CLAHE) to enhance contrast. Composite color images are converted into their luminance. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the results are generated for each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Enhances local contrast in each region of the image by applying 'Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization' (CLAHE). Composite color images are converted into their luminance. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the results are generated for each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Creates a mask that is 255 at the boundary between two labels and background.
proposals.proposed: Gets the label boundaries: it creates a mask that is 255 at the boundary between two labels and background.

proposals.current: Thresholds the image with a manual threshold. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Thresholds the 8-bit 2D image with a manually set threshold range. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Thresholds RGB images.
proposals.proposed: Manually thresholds color (RGB) images: a user-defined min/max threshold is applied to each color channel, producing a binary mask.

proposals.current: Computes Hessian the eigenvalues of the Hessian, which can be used for example to discriminate locally between plate-like, line-like, and blob-like image structures. All largest eigenvalues are put in a separate image, as are all smallest, and in 3D all middle as well. If the size of the image is unity in the z-dimension (single slice), the node computes 2D-Hessian eigenvalues, otherwise it computes 3D-Hessian eigenvalues (for each time frame and channel in a 5D image).
proposals.proposed: Computes the Hessian eigenvalue features of each image. The eigenvalues can be used to discriminate locally between plate-like, line-like, and blob-like structures; all largest, all smallest, and in 3D all middle eigenvalues are written to separate output images. If the image has a single slice, the node computes 2D-Hessian eigenvalues, otherwise 3D-Hessian eigenvalues (for each time frame and channel in a 5D image).

proposals.current: Assembles/overlays extracted ROI onto the target images. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
proposals.proposed: Assembles/overlays the extracted 2D ROI onto the target images. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.

proposals.current: Sorts the ROI list elements via statistics and allows to you extract the n top values. Optionally, line and fill colors of the output rows can be colored according to the output order. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Sorts the 2D ROI list elements via statistics and allows to you extract the n top values. Optionally, line and fill colors of the output rows can be colored according to the output order. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Splits the image into tiles of a predefined size. If the image is not perfectly tileable, it is resized.
proposals.proposed: Tiles the 2D image into tiles of a predefined size. If the image is not perfectly tileable, it is resized.

proposals.current: Merges/Assembles multiple image tiles back into one image. Utilizes annotations to determine the location of tiles. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
proposals.proposed: Un-tiling: merges/assembles multiple 2D image tiles back into one image. Utilizes annotations to determine the location of tiles. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.

proposals.current: Keeps only the largest connected component in the input mask.
proposals.proposed: Keeps only the largest connected region in the input mask.

proposals.current: Performs a Z, C, or T-Projection that selects the best-scoring pixel from the Z/C/T column. If no score image is provided, an automatically generated score is generated by either applying Sobel filter (Tenengrad), or by calculating the local variance. The resulting automatically generated score is then blurred using a Gaussian blur. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Generates an extended depth of focus projection: a Z, C, or T-projection that selects the best-scoring pixel from the Z/C/T column. If no score image is provided, an automatically generated score is generated by either applying Sobel filter (Tenengrad), or by calculating the local variance. The resulting automatically generated score is then blurred using a Gaussian blur. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Merges 2D image planes into a 3D stack. Data annotations are used to put images into groups. All images in a group are then merged into a 3D stack. The order of the stack slices is determined by the 'Slice index annotation' that is ignored while defining the groups. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
proposals.proposed: Creates a 3D stack from 2D image planes. Data annotations put images into groups; the order of the stack slices is determined by the 'Slice index annotation', which is ignored while defining the groups. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.

proposals.current: Applies a mathematical function to each pixel. Supported operations are: ABS, INVERT, SQUARE, LOGARITHM, SQRT, and EXP
proposals.proposed: Applies a pixel-wise mathematical transformation to each pixel. Supported operations are: ABS, INVERT, SQUARE, LOGARITHM, SQRT, and EXP

proposals.current: Draws one or multiple ROI that have two definition points, including lines, rectangles, and ovals. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Draws one or multiple 2D ROI that have two definition points, including lines, rectangles, and ovals. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Aligns the target image to the source image using methods implemented by TurboReg and MultiStackReg. Due to the variation in registration tasks, this node follows a 'rules' approach where each slice of the input image is matched to one rule that determines how the slice is aligned. There are three modes: (1) register to a reference slice, (2) use the same transformation calculated for another slice, and (3) apply no registration. Use the examples provided via the 'Tools' menu (top right of the parameter window) to get started with configuring the rules. Handling of RGB images: as the underlying alignment methods were only designed for greyscale images, RGB slices are automatically converted to greyscale prior to registration (using ImageJ methods). The resulting transformation is then applied per RGB channel, which is then output. Please note that if an RGB image is present, the output will be RGB. You may lose greyscale precision (16 bit/ 32 bit) in other slices. To prevent this, convert RGB to greyscale prior to registration (e.g. by splitting RGB channels into hyperstack channels). This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Aligns each 2D image to the referenced source image using the simple TurboReg registration mode, with methods from TurboReg and MultiStackReg. A rule decides per slice: register to a reference slice, reuse another slice's transformation, or skip. See the 'Tools' menu examples. RGB slices are registered as greyscale per channel, so the output stays RGB and other slices can lose 16/32 bit precision; convert RGB to greyscale first to avoid this.

proposals.current: Reorders the channels of each input image
proposals.proposed: Arranges the channels of each input image: it reorders the channels according to a channel-to-channel assignment.

proposals.current: If the input image has 3 channel axis slices, those channels are merged into one RGB slice. Useful if you imported images via Bio-Formats or other importers that automatically split channels.
proposals.proposed: Combines 3 channel axis slices into one RGB slice. Useful if you imported images via Bio-Formats or other importers that automatically split channels.

proposals.current: Slices a hyperstack via a range of indices.
proposals.proposed: Reduces and splits a hyperstack: it selects ranges of Z, channel, and frame indices, keeping the chosen slices and dropping the rest.

proposals.current: Applies a Bandpass filter
proposals.proposed: Applies an FFT bandpass filter in the frequency domain: smaller structures are filtered up to, and larger structures filtered down to, specified diameters.

proposals.current: Applies a pixel-wise mathematical operation that produces a single output image. Please note that this node applies an expression for each pixel, which has a considerable performance cost. We recommend to use 'Fast image arithmetics' instead. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Slow image arithmetics: applies a pixel-wise mathematical operation that produces a single output image. Please note that this node applies an expression for each pixel, which has a considerable performance cost. We recommend to use 'Fast image arithmetics' instead. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Outputs one table that contains the counts for each incoming ROI. Each ROI list produces one column in the output table and contains all annotations of the incoming ROI data. You can add multiple input slots. All output table column is named according to the slot name of the incoming ROI list.This node can merge ROI lists according to their annotations. The sum of the counts within the same iteration step are generated. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
proposals.proposed: Counts the 2D ROI in each incoming ROI list: each list produces one column in the output table, named after its slot. Multiple input slots are allowed. This node merges ROI lists according to their annotations, generating the sum of the counts within the same iteration step. To group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.

proposals.current: Filters the ROI list elements by the name and other basic properties.
proposals.proposed: Filters the 2D ROI list elements by the name and other basic properties via a user-written expression.

proposals.current: Removes all ROI that intersect with image borders. Use the 'Border' parameter to define a rectangle inside of the image dimensions. If a ROI is not contained within this region, it is removed. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Removes all 2D ROI that intersect with image borders. Use the 'Border' parameter to define a rectangle inside of the image dimensions. If a ROI is not contained within this region, it is removed. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Converts ROI lists to color images. The line and fill color is stored within the ROI themselves. This algorithm does not need a reference image that determines the output size.
proposals.proposed: Converts only 2D ROI to RGB: it turns 2D ROI lists into color images using the line and fill colors stored in the ROI themselves. This algorithm does not need a reference image that determines the output size.

proposals.current: Allows to implement a custom thresholding method via expressions. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Thresholds 16-bit 2D images with a custom thresholding method that you implement via expressions. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Allows to implement a custom thresholding method via expressions. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Thresholds 8-bit 2D images with a custom thresholding method that you implement via expressions. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Applies a ROI detection and measurement for each threshold value. Based on the user-provided ROI criteria the threshold is either accepted or rejected. Returns the mask with the first applicable threshold or an image with zero values. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Iteratively thresholds the 2D image so the segmented objects match your criteria: it applies ROI detection and measurement for each threshold value, accepting or rejecting it based on the user-provided ROI criteria. Returns the mask with the first applicable threshold or an image with zero values. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Allows users to draw or modify a mask that is drawn over a reference image. You can supply existing masks via the 'Masks' input. If a iteration step has no existing mask, a new one is generated according to the node parameters. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot. If items are missing, they will be generated according to this node's generator function. Otherwise data will be passed through.
proposals.proposed: Interactively lets users draw or modify a mask that is drawn over a reference image. You can supply existing masks via the 'Masks' input. If a iteration step has no existing mask, a new one is generated according to the node parameters. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot. If items are missing, they will be generated according to this node's generator function. Otherwise data will be passed through.

proposals.current: Allows users to draw or modify ROIs that are drawn over a reference image. You can supply existing masks via the 'ROI' input. If a iteration step has no existing mask, a new one is generated according to the node parameters. BROKEN! USE THE MASK DRAWER INSTEAD OR USE IMAGEJ DIRECTLY! This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot. If items are missing, they will be generated according to this node's generator function. Otherwise data will be passed through.
proposals.proposed: Interactively lets users draw or modify ROIs that are drawn over a reference image. BROKEN! USE THE MASK DRAWER INSTEAD OR USE IMAGEJ DIRECTLY! Existing ROI can be supplied via the 'ROI' input; otherwise a new mask is generated according to the node parameters. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations (one data item per slot per group). If items are missing, the generator function creates them; otherwise data is passed through.

proposals.current: Computes the distance map from a binary image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Computes a 2D Chamfer distance map from a binary image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Computes the distance map from a binary image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Computes a 3D Chamfer distance map from a binary image, using 3D Chamfer weights for the distance transform.

proposals.current: Computes the distance map from a label image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Computes a 3D Chamfer distance map from a label image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Transfers image sequences into an optic flow field. Flow fields are calculated for each pair (t,t+1) of the sequence with length |T| independently. The motion vector for each pixel in image t is estimated by searching the most similar looking pixel in image t+1. The similarity measure is the sum of square differences of all pixels in a local vicinity. The local vicinity is defined by a block and is calculated using an IntegralImage. Both the size of the block and the search radius are parameters of the method. The output is a two-channel image with (T-1) items. The pixels in each channel describe the relative location of the next similar pixel in polar coordinates (default) or cartesian coordinates.
proposals.proposed: Computes the optical flow field of an image sequence with a block-based MSE similarity measure. For each pair (t,t+1), the motion vector of every pixel is found by searching the most similar pixel in t+1, comparing the sum of square differences over a local block via an IntegralImage. Block size and search radius are parameters. Output: a two-channel image with (T-1) items, each channel giving the relative location of the next similar pixel in polar (default) or cartesian coordinates.

proposals.current: Transfers image sequences into an optic flow field. Flow fields are calculated for each pair (t,t+1) of the sequence with length |T| independently. The motion vector for each pixel in image t is estimated by searching the most similar looking pixel in image t+1. The similarity measure is the sum of differences of all pixels in a local vicinity. The local vicinity is defined by a Gaussian. Both the standard deviation of the Gaussian (the size of the local vicinity) and the search radius are parameters of the method. The output is a two-channel image with (T-1) items. The pixels in each channel describe the relative location of the next similar pixel in polar coordinates (default) or cartesian coordinates.
proposals.proposed: Computes the optical flow field of an image sequence with an MSE similarity over a Gaussian window. For each pair (t,t+1), each pixel's motion vector is found by searching the most similar pixel in t+1, comparing the sum of differences over a local window. The window size (Gaussian standard deviation) and the search radius are parameters. Output: a two-channel image with (T-1) items, each channel giving the relative location of the next similar pixel in polar (default) or cartesian coordinates.

proposals.current: Transfers image sequences into an optic flow field. Flow fields are calculated for each pair (t,t+1) of the sequence with length |T| independently. The motion vector for each pixel in image t is estimated by searching the most similar looking pixel in image t+1. The similarity measure is Pearson Product-Moment Correlation Coefficient of all pixels in a local vicinity. The local vicinity is defined by a block and is calculated using an IntegralImage. Both the size of the block and the search radius are parameters of the method. The output is a two-channel image with (T-1) items. The pixels in each channel describe the relative location of the next similar pixel in polar coordinates (default) or cartesian coordinates.
proposals.proposed: Computes the optical flow field of an image sequence with the PMCC (Pearson Product-Moment Correlation Coefficient) as MSE block similarity. For each pair (t,t+1), each pixel's motion vector is found by searching the most similar pixel in t+1, comparing a local block via an IntegralImage. Block size and search radius are parameters. Output: a two-channel image with (T-1) items, each channel giving the relative location of the next similar pixel in polar (default) or cartesian coordinates.

proposals.current: Annotates the incoming images by their statistics. The statistics are created via annotations. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Annotates the incoming images with statistics that you compute via a user-written expression. The statistics are created via annotations. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Applies the OrientationJ vector field calculation algorithm
proposals.proposed: Computes the 2D orientation vector field of each image using the OrientationJ vector field calculation algorithm

proposals.current: Tags all pixel/voxels in a skeleton image and then counts all its junctions, triple and quadruple points and branches, and measures their average and maximum length. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Analyzes 2D/3D skeleton images: it tags all pixel/voxels in a skeleton image and then counts all its junctions, triple and quadruple points and branches, and measures their average and maximum length. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and integrated, thus allowing to generate histograms. Allows the generation of normalized and cumulative histograms. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Generates key/value histograms from 5D data: this node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and integrated, thus allowing to generate histograms. Allows the generation of normalized and cumulative histograms. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. Buckets the pixels of the 'Value' image based on the pixel in the 'Key' and calculates the number of values, their sum, and the average value. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Fast key/value statistics for 5D data: this node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. Buckets the pixels of the 'Value' image based on the pixel in the 'Key' and calculates the number of values, their sum, and the average value. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The set of value pixels is partitioned into two sets based on whether the key is lower, or equal/higher than the currently processed key. One or multiple values can be created for each partitioning. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Generates key/value threshold statistics from 5D data: it consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The set of value pixels is partitioned into two sets depending on whether the key is lower, or equal/higher than the currently processed key. One or multiple values can be created per partitioning. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and then integrated for each threshold in the key image. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Generates threshold/value statistics from 5D data: this node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and then integrated for each threshold in the key image. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and then integrated for each threshold in the key image. This variant uses table column integration functions that are faster than expression-based operations. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Fast variant of the threshold/value statistics for 5D data: it consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and integrated for each threshold in the key image, via table column integration functions that are faster than expression-based operations. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations; those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and then integrated for each threshold in the key image. This variant is hardcoded to calculate the average of the pixels per threshold. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Fast, average variant of the threshold/value statistics for 5D data: it consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and then integrated for each threshold in the key image. It is hardcoded to calculate the average of the pixels per threshold. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

proposals.current: Converts a greyscale image into a binary image. All pixels with a value larger than zero are set to 255.
proposals.proposed: Binarizes a greyscale image into a binary mask: all pixels with a value larger than zero are set to 255.
